title: The 1928 football team
caption: Fred Beresford’s 1928 team brought a new generation onto Stackpole’s Field. The yearbook recalls forty-five candidates but only two returning varsity men, captain Reggie Goss and Gilman Cann, and describes a squad whose oldest player was seventeen. Carroll Freeman, Red Hunnewell, Stuart Kidder and Jim Foley emerge as central figures in its account of hard work and determined play. Kidder, a first-year player who became the leading ground-gainer, provided a memorable Thanksgiving highlight with a pass to Goss that gained more than sixty yards. Saugus lost that muddy finale to Mission High of Roxbury, 6–0, but the yearbook honored the seniors’ effort and the resolve of a team that kept fighting against heavier opposition. The original portrait and two newly added review pages preserve the players, their positions, the Thanksgiving game and the hopes placed in the next generation. The seven wins in eleven games mentioned in the opening historical passage belong to 1927, not the 1928 season.

images.title: 1928 season review · a young team under Fred Beresford
images.caption: The yearbook traces the senior class’s football experience from 1925 through 1928. After a 1927 team coached by Benny Rice won seven of eleven games, Fred Beresford returned for 1928. Forty-five candidates answered the call, but Reggie Goss and Gilman Cann were the only returning varsity men identified at the outset. Goss was elected captain. images.title: 1928 Thanksgiving · a determined stand in the mud
images.caption: On Thanksgiving morning at Stackpole’s Field, Saugus faced the heavier Mission High team from Roxbury on a surface covered by three or four inches of mud. Mission won 6–0, but the yearbook praised Saugus’s effort before the season’s largest home crowd. Stuart Kidder’s pass to Reggie Goss produced a gain of more than sixty yards. Freeman, Hunnewell and Goss anchored a stubborn left side, while Kidder, Kelley and Jim Foley earned praise in the backfield. Foley, who played with one arm, was singled out for his tackling, passing and spirit. The page also records the first-string lineup and looks ahead to captain-elect Ernie Castle and returning players Lawrence Templeman, Jimmy Glinski, Mike Gifford and Bill MacKay.

title: The 1929 football team
caption: Coach Rice’s 1929 Sachems began with consecutive shutout victories over Manchester and Swampscott. The 12–0 Swampscott result was especially significant: the yearbook described it as Saugus’s first victory over that rival. Templeman supplied the finishing runs, while Roveto’s passing and the receiving of Gates and Quint helped move the offense. Injuries and a demanding schedule tested the team, including captain Quint’s knee injury against Milton and tackle Ed Newbury’s broken wrist at Chelsea. A 27–6 victory over Rockport showcased Templeman’s big-play running, with touchdown runs of 70, 44 and 35 yards. The squad portrait and companion game account, published in the 1930 Tontoquonian, offer a detailed view of the preceding fall’s players and performances. The supplied results page ends with Chelsea and does not document the complete season record.

images.title: 1929 season · game-by-game yearbook account
images.caption: Published in the 1930 Tontoquonian, this page reviews the preceding fall. Saugus opened September 28 at Stackpole’s Field with a 22–0 victory over Manchester: Templeman scored twice, Gifford once, and Gates added a safety. A 12–0 victory over Swampscott followed, described by the yearbook as Saugus’s first football win over that opponent. Roveto’s passing to Gates and Quint helped set up one Templeman touchdown; Templeman later added a 25-yard scoring run. Losses followed against Milton (15–0), Essex Aggies (15–0) and Reading (12–0). Saugus rebounded against Rockport, 27–6, with Templeman scoring on runs of 70, 44 and 35 yards and Muzzey adding another touchdown. Chelsea won the next recorded game, 24–6, with Templeman scoring for Saugus. Captain Quint injured his right knee against Milton, while tackle Ed Newbury broke his right wrist against Chelsea. This page does not include the Danvers result or establish the complete season record.

title: The 1930 football team
caption: Led by captain Jim Muzzy and Coach Rice, the 1930 Sachems were celebrated in their yearbook as Saugus’s best football team since the undefeated 1922 squad. A 30–0 opening victory over Manchester set the tone, while Laurie Templeman’s speed and scoring and Muzzy’s passing, tackling and steady leadership gave the backfield its character. Rice’s tribute also recognized Jimmie Glinski, Albie Day, Harry Raddin, Eddie Newbury, Stewart Quint, Foster and Gordon Baker, emphasizing the line play, blocking and persistence behind the team’s success. The squad photograph commemorates a 14–0 victory over Danvers with a handwritten 1930 notation. Its printed “Football Squad of 1931” caption reflects a dating difference retained in the image and explained here; the gallery follows the 1930 season identification supplied by Sal Nicolo. Beyond the games, the review honors the cheerleaders and recalls a Parent Teachers’ Association banquet at which nine seniors received sweaters and returning players received letters. Together, the portrait and written tribute preserve a season remembered for strong play, shared effort and community pride. The supplied page does not establish an exact final season record.

Rice praised Jimmie Glinski’s strength in the line, Albie Day at center, Harry Raddin at offensive end, Eddie Newbury’s determination despite an injured wrist, and Stewart Quint’s steady improvement at tackle. title: The 1939 Sachems · a season to remember
caption: The 1939 North Shore champions. The 1939 Sachems gave Saugus a season to remember. Under head coach Charles “Buzz” Harvey and assistant Nick Morris, a team that began amid modest expectations answered a 12–0 opening defeat at Medford with ten unbeaten games, finishing 9–1–1. Co-captains Jimmy Duffy and Stan Green helped lead a squad whose resilience, teamwork and determined play earned growing recognition across the region. Mike Harrington, Eddie Shipulski, Fred Walkey, Ray Mansfield, Dexter Pratt, Joe Bucherie, Woody Dill and Del Pitman figure prominently in the yearbook’s accounts, while the named squad portrait preserves Art Statuto and the teammates whose contributions made the season possible. Shutout victories over Gloucester, Swampscott and Marblehead built momentum, but the defining afternoon came against Salem. Before a crowd the yearbook estimated at 10,000, Saugus prevailed 3–0 on Bucherie’s field goal, with Harrington holding, backed by a defense that kept the Witches scoreless. A 38–6 Thanksgiving victory over Danvers provided a fitting farewell for the seniors. The celebration reached beyond the field: supporters traveled to Gloucester by special train, the squad enjoyed a Christmas holiday trip to New York and West Point, and 1,000 fans attended the January 20 banquet at the Lynn Armory. These seven yearbook pages preserve more than scores. Together, the action photographs, roster, co-captain portraits and celebrations honor a team that turned an uncertain beginning into an enduring source of Sachem pride—and the community that stood behind it.

title: The 1953 North Shore champions · team & season review
caption: The 1953 Sachems earned their place in Saugus football history as North Shore champions, led by co-captains John Leahy and Doug MacNeill under coach John Janusas. These seven yearbook pages bring together the full squad and named roster, player portraits set against newspaper headlines, detailed game accounts and three collections of photographs from the field and stands. The season demanded both resilience and teamwork. Saugus opened with shutouts of Revere and Lynn Classical, rallied for a 12–12 tie with Marblehead, and edged Beverly 14–13 in a game the yearbook remembered as a thriller. A 26–18 victory over Lynn English kept the Sachems moving forward before Chelsea delivered their only regular-season defeat. They answered with a 27–0 win over Salem, then finished decisively on Thanksgiving, defeating Peabody 33–6 to secure the North Shore League title. Billy MacNeill, Bill Whittredge, Bob Piwowarski, Mal Rice and Charlie and Jackie Lawrence feature throughout the accounts, alongside the linemen and teammates who made the scoring drives and defensive stops possible. The yearbook records a 6–1–1 season and lists the 18–6 Joyce Jamboree loss to Haverhill separately. Together, these pages honor the players, coaches, managers, band and supporters who shared in a memorable championship autumn.
dateSource: Contributed yearbook pages explicitly describe the 1953 North Shore championship season.

title: The 1954 Sachems · squad, co-captains & season review
caption: The 1954 Sachems finished 6–3 under head coach John Janusas, with co-captains Jack Lawrence and Malcolm “Mal” Rice leading a squad whose season combined strong running, determined line play and a winning Thanksgiving finish. Saugus opened by shutting out Revere, 20–0, and went on to beat Marblehead, Chelsea, Amesbury and Winthrop before closing with a 20–12 victory at Peabody. The nine printed results total 171 points for Saugus and 98 for its opponents. Rice and Bob Piwowarski feature prominently in the running accounts, while Charlie Lawrence’s passing, Fred Case’s long runs and Paul Downing’s receiving and timely fumble recovery appear throughout the review. The yearbook also celebrates the work of Billy Ellis, Bob Lancaster, Tommy Mullen, Ed Olley, Fred Bradley, Ted Dwyer, Ken Ballard and Fred MacDonald in the line. A 77-yard run by Case against Lynn English, Rice’s 71-yard score against Chelsea, and Fred Orlando’s 92-yard touchdown against Winthrop preserve some of the season’s most memorable individual plays. These six pages bring together the full schedule, a named team portrait, co-captain portraits, individual player studies and action photographs from the jamboree and regular season. They also preserve the community around the team and a Thanksgiving farewell to the graduating players. The printed 1954–1955 heading denotes the school year; this gallery group records the fall 1954 football season.
dateSource: Contributed yearbook pages; fall 1954 season identified by Sal Nicolo and the printed results.

Against Lynn English, Fred Case broke a 77-yard run and Bob Piwowarski added a later touchdown in a 27–13 defeat. At Chelsea, Paul Downing’s recovery at the Chelsea 38 set up a Piwowarski score; Rice later ran 71 yards for the second touchdown in a 12–0 win. A 41–0 victory over Winthrop featured scoring by Case, Piwowarski, Charlie Lawrence and Rice, as well as a 92-yard touchdown run by Fred Orlando in the second half.

title: Saugus in an underdog role · 1998 Thanksgiving preview
caption:
Joyce Erekson’s Daily Evening Item preview spotlights the 1998 Sachems ahead of Thanksgiving against Peabody. Raphael Zammit entered the finale with a school-record 21 touchdowns, surpassing L.J. McKanas’s previous mark of 20. He had rushed for 1,341 yards on 210 carries and added 400 receiving yards. His touchdowns included 18 rushing, two receiving and an interception return; he scored five against Winthrop. At strong safety, Zammit recorded seven sacks, 43 tackles, eight hurries and two interceptions.

Senior quarterback Ryan Lahey completed 43 of 82 passes for 825 yards and seven touchdowns, added five rushing touchdowns and contributed at free safety. Linebacker/fullback Mike Panzini recorded 130 tackles, four interceptions and four fumble recoveries, along with a touchdown. Matt Wass had five interceptions and caught 36 passes for two touchdowns, averaging 11.7 yards per reception.

The article also recognizes tackle Pat Ross, tight end Garrett DiCarlo, linemen Murray Wadman and Brian Mirasolo, center Brett Poindexter, tackle Jason Katsos, and kicker/punter Michael Lush. These totals were reported before the Thanksgiving finale, not as final season statistics.
